sections.heading: Hero
sections.body: An island-scale mixed climbing destination with coastal limestone, granite, sport crags, multi-pitches, trad-style venues and deep-water soloing.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.body:
Sardinia is too broad to read as one crag. Treat it as an island climbing trip: coastal limestone, inland sectors, granite areas and sea-cliff venues spread across a large Mediterranean island.

That variety is the point. A Sardinia trip can be sport climbing, multi-pitch climbing, deep-water soloing or a road-trip mix between bases, but it needs more planning than a single village destination.

sections.heading: Rock and climbing character
sections.body:
The supported rock types are limestone and granite. The limestone gives sport crags, sea cliffs, steep walls and slabs, while the granite broadens the island beyond the usual Mediterranean limestone picture.

Because the island is large, style depends heavily on the chosen base. Cala Gonone, Capo Caccia, Osilo and other areas should eventually be handled with more granular local detail.

sections.heading: Who it suits
sections.body:
Sardinia suits climbers who want variety and are happy to plan around a large island. It is strong for sport climbers, multi-pitch teams and climbers interested in sea-cliff or deep-water soloing days.

It is less useful as a plug-and-play beginner page until the destination is split into clear bases with current route and accommodation detail.

sections.heading: Season and conditions
sections.body: Spring and autumn are the conservative climbing seasons. Summer stays marked as an avoid season for serious climbing because heat and sun exposure can dominate unless you are targeting very specific aspects or water-based objectives.

sections.heading: Transport and access
sections.body: Sardinia requires flight or ferry access, then a car for the climbing itself. Distances between areas are too large to treat the island as a walkable crag cluster.

sections.heading: Rest days
sections.body: Rest days are one of Sardinia's strengths: beaches, coastal towns, hiking and food can all sit naturally between climbing days. The exact options depend on whether the trip is based around the north, east coast or a wider island loop.

sections.heading: FAQ
sections.body:
Is Sardinia one climbing area? No. It is an island-scale destination with several distinct climbing bases.

What styles are supported here? Sport climbing, multi-pitch climbing, deep-water soloing and trad-style venues.

Do you need a car? Yes. A car is the practical default for moving between climbing areas.
